content:
The test image shows two tomato plant stems pulled from soil, displaying longitudinal brown/tan discoloration in the vascular tissue from the root upward. Roots appear brown and damaged. No white mycelium or sclerotia visible. This points to a vascular wilt disease — most likely Verticillium Wilt (vascular discoloration visible when stems are viewed longitudinally) or Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

Let me check a Verticillium Wilt reference image.

The reference Verticillium Wilt image shows leaf symptoms (yellowing, wilting). But the test image shows the stem/root area with longitudinal brown vascular streaking — which is the definitive internal stem symptom of Verticillium Wilt ("brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut lengthwise"). The bleached tan stems with brown vascular streaks running from root upward, with damaged brown roots, matches this classic diagnostic feature. No white mycelium (ruling out Sclerotinia/Southern Blight), no pith streaming (Southern Bacterial Wilt would show slimy bacterial ooze), and no concentric rings (ruling out Alternaria).

No white mycelium, sclerotia, or concentric canker rings are visible, ruling out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia, and Alternaria.
